newsitem.title: USA: Airline stocks off amid profit-taking, fuel rise.
newsitem.headline: Airline stocks off amid profit-taking, fuel rise.

text.p: Airline stocks weakened Wednesday amid a strong wave of profit-taking and a slight increase in jet fuel prices, analysts said.

"Oil prices are up a bit ... but it dosen't strike me that there's anything more sinister than airline stocks taking a rest after a big run-up during the past fortnight," said Timothy Ross, an airline analyst with SBC Warburg.
The Dow Jones Transportation Average lost 41 to 2428.59. Continental Airlines Inc lost 1-1/2 to 32, while Delta Air Lines shed 2-3/8 to 85-3/8.

Transportation stocks, historically underperformers, have outperformed the broader market since the beginning of the year. The Dow Jones transportation index has posted a 7.7 percent gain, compared with a 6.4 percent increase for the Dow industrials and 5.7 percent gain for the S&P 500.
Airline stocks surged two weeks ago, after UAL Corp issued a bullish forecast for first quarter earnings.
Since then, several brokerage firms upgraded airline stocks, citing higher demand, increased load factors and lower fuel costs than last year.
After last year's 30 percent surge in global jet fuel prices, airlines had a reprieve at the start of 1997 as prices eased.
Although jet fuel prices still remain below last year's level, prices have increased slightly during the past week, NatWest Securities analyst Susan Donofrio said in a research report.

The industry's labor woes also appear to be easing, analysts said. United Airlines recently reached a labor agreement with its pilots, ending some uncertainty hanging over the carrier. AMR Corp's American Airlines also is inching toward a tentative pact with its pilots.
Other transportation stocks also slipped Wednesday.

Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp said it expects its first quarter results to fall about 20 percent below last year's earnings of $1.21 a share. Burlington Northern's stock was down 1-3/8 to 81 before trading was halted ahead of the company's earnings warning.
Other railway companies also fell. CSX Corp lost two to 48 and Norfolk Southern Corp eased 2-1/8 to 92-1/2. Trucking company Yellow Corp slipped 5/8 to 16-5/8.
This slight jump in jet fuel prices may have spooked investors who have been spoiled by declining prices, analysts said.
"Oil prices have popped lately. There was a bigger drop in inventory than many expected," said Glenn Engel, an airline analyst with Goldman Sachs.

Despite Wednesday's easing in stock prices, "everything is gangbusters at the airlines," Engel said. Traffic remains strong despite a four percent increase in fares and capacity is increasing at a controlled rate.
